summary: H5 is not refuted, but only with a change to the tool. Without it, retiring per-language components is unsafe, and it fails quietly rather than loudly. With the unmodified tool, a project that took ReadmeQuick_<lang> copies from 4.44.0 keeps them after the upgrade, after `target add` and after `package update`. Generation keeps calling those copies, so the shared section never appears. Doctor labels them "additive (project-owned, not drift)" even though the copy record shows an add wrote them. `target remove` refuses them as "what `target add` did not write". A second hazard sits under that: deleting the .ts source is not enough. `tsc --build src` leaves .sdk/dist/cmp/<t>/ReadmeQuick_<t>.js behind, and the loader requires dist, so the retired component is still called. The fix is 136 added and 14 removed lines in 4 files (target.ts +85/-3, doctor.ts +45/-10, edition.ts +5/-1, remove.ts +1), plus a 143-line test file. After it, an unchanged copy that the scaffold no longer ships is reported once as RETIRED: doctor fails, it is counted as outdated, and generate warns. The next `target add`, `package update` or `edition add` deletes it and its compiled output, and the record forgets it. An edited copy is kept, still called, and reported as an `override`; doctor stays ok and does not fail because of it. A file the record does not name is never deleted. A dry run deletes nothing. Overwrite mode and --force treat an edited retired copy like any edited copy, which means they delete it. Aliases (go~go2) and a pack that retires its own component (dart) go through the same path, and both work. The language pack, still shipping its own ReadmeQuick_<lang>, generates the same output and passes its suite against the modified build, because the shared component calls a target's own component first. Two things remain open. A project with no copy record (or whose copies were never recorded) cannot be cleaned automatically; doctor now names those files, but they stay in use. And a project that deletes an override by hand leaves stale compiled output that is silently still used.

aliases: `target add go~go2` copies the scaffold's src/cmp/go tree through aliasCmpTree, so Syntax_go.ts becomes src/cmp/go2/Syntax_go2.ts. Its object content is unchanged (`lang: 'go'`), because aliasCmpText rewrites only `_go'` import suffixes and src/cmp/go/ paths. The shared component loads ./cmp/go2/Syntax_go2 by the target name and finds it: generation wrote '<!-- shared-quick provider=go --> SHARED QUICK START for go2'. The retired ReadmeQuick_go2.ts is recorded under its alias path, so retirement needs the source file list renamed with aliasCmpName before comparing. pruneRetired does that, and doctor already did (renameCmp). Measured: doctor reports RETIRED for src/cmp/go2/ReadmeQuick_go2.ts, the re-add removes it, and the shared section appears. A provider that needs to know it is serving an alias is not covered. It would get the origin's literal values, which is correct for syntax.
override_rule: An edited copy of a retired component is the project's own override, decided by the copy record and nothing else. If the recorded fingerprint differs from the file, it is an override: kept by every add and package update, called first (a target's own <Name>_<t> wins over the shared section, as for packs), and reported by doctor as `override` without failing it. `remove` refuses it, as it refuses any changed or project-added copy, unless --force is passed. An add deletes it only where any changed copy would be overwritten (--force, or main.kit.copies 'overwrite'), and then deletes its compiled output too. A file with no record entry is never deleted and is reported as additive, '(used instead of the shared <Name>)'. The advice for dropping an override must name both the source and .sdk/dist/cmp/<t>/<Name>_<t>.js, or the compiled output keeps being used. Better still, a loader or doctor check for compiled components with no source, which I did not build. Order for a PROJECT when a release retires components: (1) before upgrading, make sure every copy is recorded: any add or `package update` on a version of 4.34.0 or later records what it writes; commit .sdk/log/copies.jsonl. (2) Install the new sdkgen. (3) Run `voxgig-sdkgen doctor`: RETIRED files will be removed; decide on each `override`; additive '(used instead of the shared X)' lines are copies with no record, to delete by hand together with their dist .js. (4) Run `voxgig-sdkgen package update @voxgig/sdkgen`, which removes the unchanged retired copies and their compiled output without --force. (5) Run `npm run generate`, review the README diff, and commit. Order for a PACK AUTHOR: (1) Nothing is required while the pack keeps shipping <Name>_<lang>: output is unchanged and the suite passes against the new sdkgen. (2) To move, add the syntax provider and delete <Name>_<lang>.ts in the same release. Raise the @voxgig/sdkgen peer floor and engines.sdkgen to the first sdkgen that has both the shared component and this record-based pruning; below that, a project's old copy is called forever, labelled additive, and refused by remove. (3) Tell consumers to run `package update <pack>`. One constraint on sdkgen: the shared component must keep calling <Name>_<t> first, and OPTIONAL_COMPONENTS must keep the name, for as long as any pack or project ships one.

risks: Stale compiled output, not fixed. The loader requires .sdk/dist/cmp/<t>/<Name>_<t>.js and the project's `tsc --build src` never deletes the output of a deleted source. The change deletes it when an add prunes a copy. But a person who deletes a component (an override, or an unrecorded retired copy) by hand keeps getting it, and doctor reports nothing (measured: 'PROJECT-EDITED QUICK START' after deletion, doctor ok). Needs either a loader rule (ignore a dist module whose .sdk/src source is absent) or a doctor check for orphan compiled components.

Projects without a copy record (last add before 4.34.0, or copies never recorded) cannot be cleaned automatically. The retired copy stays, keeps overriding the shared section, and keeps any defect it carries. So any catalogue fix made once in a shared sentence (H3) does not reach that project until a person deletes the file.

Doctor exits non-zero for unchanged retired copies until the next add, like `outdated`. A CI job that gates on doctor turns red on the upgrade commit and green after `package update`. That is intended, but it is a rollout-ordering cost.

The CLI's drift summary (bin/voxgig-sdkgen) prints only forked, edited, stale and missing counts. A release that only retires files makes doctor exit 1 while printing '0 forked, 0 edited, 0 stale, 0 missing'. This already happens for outdated-only drift. Read in the code, not run in that exact state.

The generate warning says '3 file(s) in .sdk differ … changed in this project' for files that are MISSING (the new providers). This is existing wording, made more visible because each retirement also adds a provider.

Under --force or overwrite mode, an edited retired copy is deleted with no backup, as an edited live copy is overwritten. That is consistent with those modes, but the edit is lost, with nothing left to merge into.
Edition component retirement shares the code but was not exercised end to end.

The 'own component wins' precedence is what keeps packs working, and it is the same precedence that hides an un-pruned retired copy. Any later change that makes the shared section ignore <Name>_<t> would break every pack that has not moved.
An override is reported on every doctor run but never fails it. A project can carry an outdated override indefinitely without noticing that shared fixes are not reaching it.
surprises: Doctor calls an unchanged retired copy 'additive (project-owned, not drift)' although .sdk/log/copies.jsonl holds its fingerprint from the add that wrote it. The record could always tell the two apart; doctor never asked it for a file the scaffold does not ship.
`target remove` refuses an unchanged retired copy with the message 'refusing to delete what `target add` did not write', which the record contradicts.

In row 1 the exit status changed because of the MISSING new providers, not the retired files. A release that only deleted components would leave doctor at exit 0 and generation silently on the old text.
pruneStaleTemplates exists but covers tm/ only, and on tm/ it deletes edited files regardless of the record. src/cmp had no pruning at all.

The copy-merge guard (merge mode) already holds back an unlink of an unrecorded file and defers the deletion of an edited one. The record check in pruneRetired is therefore the only protection under --force and overwrite mode, where the guard is off.
target models already declare `superseded:` for retired GENERATED output (doctor prune), but there is no equivalent for retired components.

Building a scratch project with `declaration: true` through symlinked jostraca failed with TS2883 ('cannot be named … not portable'). This is an artifact of the symlinked toolchain; the scratch projects compile with declaration off.

hypotheses.evidence: Not refuted, but only because of the change. With the stand-in and no change, retirement is unsafe in a quiet way: old copies stay in use after re-add and package update, doctor mislabels them as additive, remove refuses them, and stale dist output survives deleting the source. With the 136/-14-line change, the rules hold. Add is overwrite (the source's deletion is applied). Doctor compares everything an add writes (retired and override categories). Deletion is limited to what the record shows an add wrote and left unchanged. Dry run writes nothing. Junk is filtered through the existing walk, and aliases are renamed by the existing aliasCmpName. All rows except hand-deletion pass. The langpack's targets generate byte-identical .md and its suite passes (74/76, 2 skipped, same as before). Conditions: projects must have a copy record, and hand-deleting a component still leaves stale compiled output in use.
